claim: Creates running at the same time all pass the drafts-per-hour count before any of them inserts, so a caller with a valid token gets past ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR just by sending the creates in parallel.
evidence: drafts.py:112-134 counts with get_list and then inserts in a separate await, with no lock or reservation in between. The server is stateless and async, so each parallel tools/call POST runs this sequence interleaved with the others. I ran a scratch test (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/race/test_race.py) with settings(max_drafts_per_hour='2'), FakeErpnext(delay=0.05) and the frozen clock. It ran 6 create_draft_sales_invoice calls at once through tools._run, using different quantities so the duplicate check doesn't apply. All 6 succeeded and 6 POSTs reached the fake. Sequentially, the third call is refused (test_the_limit_counts_the_drafts_enterich_creates). An agent steered by outside text, or caught in a loop, that issues parallel tool calls (MCP clients do this on their own) creates as many drafts as it sends concurrently, which is the failure REQ-001-URS-F010 exists to prevent. The backlog and analysis 001 don't list it; it isn't 'sheer volume' DoS, because 6 calls break a limit of 2.
proposal: Test: in the integration suite, with the limited fixture and erp.slow on the Sales Invoice resource path, start DRAFTS_PER_HOUR+1 creates at once (anyio task group over tools._run, or concurrent client calls) and assert that at most DRAFTS_PER_HOUR inserts reach the fake and the rest return LIMITED. Fix: serialise count-then-insert per DocType inside the process, with an anyio.Lock per DocType held across the count and the insert. Also count creates already in flight in this process. State in the configuration guide that the limit holds per Enterich instance, so a deployment runs one replica or accepts N times the limit.

verdict.reproduction: I ran the finder's scratch test /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/race/test_race.py with `PYTHONPATH=/home/ubuntu/dev/enterich uv run pytest -s`. Setup: settings(max_drafts_per_hour='2', timezone=TIMEZONE), FakeErpnext(delay=0.05) with the frozen clock. It starts 6 create_draft_sales_invoice calls (qty 1..6, so the duplicate check doesn't apply) at once through tools._run in an anyio task group. All 6 returned is_error=False (ACC-SINV-2026-00101..00106), and 6 POSTs to /api/resource/Sales Invoice reached the fake. For a control I ran the same scenario one call at a time (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/race/test_seq.py). There 2 succeed, the other 4 are refused with 'The agent user created 2 sales invoices in the last hour, the most the operator ...', and 2 POSTs reach the fake. So the fake does count Enterich's own inserts, and only running the calls at once gets past the limit of 2.
verdict.reason: src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:109-134 (insert) counts with get_list and only then inserts, in a separate await, with nothing that serialises the two. Creates running at the same time in one process all see the count below the limit before any of them inserts. In scope: SECURITY.md:25 names 'getting past ... the configured limit of drafts per hour (ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR)'. This is not the out-of-scope 'sheer volume' DoS (SECURITY.md:36), because 6 calls break a limit of 2. Not listed as open: docs/backlog/backlog.md:13 only lists the separate amount ceiling. Not intended by the specs: REQ-001-PRS-F019 says a create SHALL refuse once the count reaches the limit, and the archived ITEM-008 says the count should hold 'across replicas and restarts', so a limit beaten by parallel calls goes against the design. No current test runs creates in parallel; test_the_limit_counts_the_drafts_enterich_creates (tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:1199) runs them one after another. Class is fix: an anyio.Lock per DocType held across the count and the insert closes the reproduced breach within one process, and no spec or ADR has to change for that. The suggested note in the configuration guide that the limit holds per instance would be a guide change, and that part is a proposal. The test belongs in tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py next to the existing limit tests (limited fixture, slow fake, DRAFTS_PER_HOUR+1 creates at once, at most DRAFTS_PER_HOUR POSTs).

claim: The improvement pipeline pushes `auto/` branches to the public repository with no secret scan at any point: the gate runs none, and CI's gitleaks job never runs on a push to a branch that has no pull request, so a secret a fix agent commits is public and nobody scans it.
evidence: Steps: (1) a fix agent working in the operator's environment writes a credential into a test or fixture under tests/ or src/enterich/. The credential could be the seeded e2e site's api_key/api_secret (tests/e2e/conftest.py:46-53), a value from a local .env, or one copied from text it read. It commits that as `test:`/`fix:` on `auto/tests-...`. (2) `harness/gate.py --push` runs only ruff, format, basedpyright, mdformat, links and pytest (CHECKS, harness/gate.py:83-90), and its path rules (ALLOWED/FORBIDDEN, :41-81) say nothing about file content. A passing branch is then pushed with `git push origin <commit>:refs/heads/auto/...` (pushed(), :358-366). (3) `.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6` triggers on `pull_request` and on `push` to `main` only, so the `secrets` job (ci.yml:76-94, gitleaks) never runs for the pushed auto/ branch. ADR-008 forbids the pipeline to merge but says nothing about opening a PR, so the branch stays unscanned until an operator opens one. Even then gitleaks only reports a secret that is already public. AGENTS.md's 'Secrets never in Git' and ADR-008:112 ('no secrets') are not enforced on the one path that commits and pushes without a person. I checked that gitleaks' default rules do flag ERPNext-shaped key/secret pairs (`generic-api-key` on `erpnext_api_key="..."`, `token k:s`, and `ENTERICH_ERPNEXT_API_SECRET=...`): the scan would catch the secret if it ran before the push.
proposal: Close it: add a `secrets` check to CHECKS in harness/gate.py that runs gitleaks (the pinned .github/gitleaks image) over `origin/main..<commit>` with `--redact` and fails the branch on any finding, so a branch with a leak is never pushed. Also widen ci.yml's `push` trigger to `auto/**` (or all branches) so pushed branches are scanned without a PR. Test: in tests/repo/test_harness.py, a branch whose commit adds `erpnext_api_secret = "<fake secret, redacted>"` under tests/ fails the gate's checks and `pushed()` is not called.

verdict.reproduction: I wrote a throwaway pytest at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/secscan/test_secret_push.py and ran it with `uv run --with pyyaml pytest -s`. It imports harness/gate.py and sets up a scratch repo with a local bare `origin`. On `auto/tests-leak` it adds the commit `test: leak`, which writes tests/test_leak.py containing `erpnext_api_secret = "<fake secret, redacted>"` and an api_key. The test asserts four things: (1) `gate.problems("auto/tests-leak", ["test: leak"], paths)` returns [], so the path and commit rules pass the branch; (2) no entry in `gate.CHECKS` is a secret scan; (3) `gate.pushed(work, commit, "auto/tests-leak")` returns True and the remote then holds the secret in plain text (`git show` in origin.git); (4) ci.yml's `on.push.branches == ["main"]`, so the `secrets` job does not run on a push of an auto/ branch that has no PR. I then ran the locally cached `gitleaks:latest` image with `--network none` over `origin/main..HEAD`. It reported "leaks found: 2" and exited non-zero. Result: 1 passed. The gate passes and pushes the leaking branch, and gitleaks would have caught the leak if anything ran it before the push.
verdict.reason:
What the code does matches the finding. harness/gate.py:83-90 CHECKS runs only ruff, format, basedpyright, mdformat, links and pytest. problems() (:191-236) only checks names and paths, never file content. pushed() (:358-366) pushes the commit straight to origin. .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6 triggers on pull_request and on push to main only, so the gitleaks `secrets` job (ci.yml:76-94) never sees a pushed auto/ branch that has no PR. There is no pre-commit or git hook in the repo either. ADR-008:106 lets the pipeline push auto/ branches with no person involved, and ADR-008:112 applies AGENTS.md's "Secrets never in Git" to it, but no check enforces that on this path. The repository is public (AGENTS.md), so a pushed secret is published before any scan.

Nothing scopes this out. SECURITY.md does not exclude it: its "Secret handling" item covers a key or secret appearing "anywhere else outside Enterich", and the promise here is AGENTS.md's. docs/backlog/backlog.md does not list it. No spec or ADR says the behaviour is intended.

Why class fix: a secrets check added to CHECKS that runs the already-pinned .github/gitleaks image over base..commit with --redact closes it within ADR-008, which already says the gate runs every check before a push. It needs no spec, ADR, guide or dependency change. Its test goes in tests/repo/test_harness.py, where the gate's push tests live (e.g. :685, :1207). Note that harness/ is outside what the pipeline itself may change (ADR-008:107), so the operator applies the gate change. Widening ci.yml's push trigger to auto/** is optional extra hardening and touches .github/.

claim: The tests only check that true loopback hosts are allowed. If _is_loopback were weakened to treat any IP literal, or any host starting with "localhost", as loopback, no test would fail, so http issuer, JWKS and resource URLs to other hosts would load and no warning would appear.
evidence: Every non-loopback http case in tests/unit/test_config.py uses a DNS name (id.example.com, erp.internal), which goes through the ValueError branch. The IP branch only ever sees loopback addresses (127.0.0.1, [::1]), and the only name-based loopback case is exactly "localhost" (test_http_urls_are_allowed_for_loopback_hosts). I replaced _is_loopback with a version that returns True for any parseable IP and for host.startswith("localhost"). load() then accepted ENTERICH_ISSUER=http://10.0.0.5/realms/x and ENTERICH_JWKS_URL=http://localhost.attacker.example/certs (checked in a scratch script). The same mutant would also hide the warning for http://10.0.0.5 as ERPNext URL. None of the tests listed for REQ-002-PRS-NF005 uses an http URL to a non-loopback IP or to a look-alike localhost name.
proposal: Add parametrized cases expecting HTTPS_ONLY for ISSUER/JWKS_URL values http://10.0.0.5/..., http://0.0.0.0/... and http://localhost.example.com/.... Add a case that http://10.0.0.5:8080 as ERPNEXT_URL produces the 'uses http' warning.

verdict.reproduction: I copied the tracked files to the scratchpad at .../scratchpad/mut. In the copy I changed _is_loopback (src/enterich/config.py:315) to return True for host.startswith("localhost") and for any IP that parses. Then I ran pytest tests/unit tests/integration with PYTHONPATH set to the copy's src, and checked that enterich.config was imported from the copy. Result: 1093 passed, 0 failed.
verdict.reason: REQ-002-PRS-NF005 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:163) says plain http is allowed only for a loopback host, for the issuer, JWKS and resource URLs, and that an http ERPNext URL to a host that isn't loopback logs a warning. _is_loopback (config.py:315-323) is the one check behind both rules (config.py:268 and 143). In tests/unit/test_config.py, the non-loopback http cases use only DNS names: id.example.com at lines 121-122, and erp.internal for the warning at about line 207. Only loopback addresses ever reach the IP branch: 127.0.0.1 and [::1] at lines 185-187. Nothing in tests/e2e or tests/repo checks loopback. The weakened version passes every unit and integration test, so the finding stands as unproven. It is not in the backlog and not out of scope. A fix within the current spec: add HTTPS_ONLY cases for http://10.0.0.5/..., http://0.0.0.0/... and http://localhost.example.com/... as ISSUER or JWKS_URL, and expect the "uses http" warning for http://10.0.0.5:8080 as ERPNEXT_URL. None of the three listed patterns fits: this is an untested loopback rule, not a yes/no comparison, a dropped argument or a check on part of a text.

claim: No test checks that a plain-http resource URL to a non-loopback host stops Enterich. The https-only rule for ENTERICH_RESOURCE_URL could be dropped and every test would still pass.
evidence: The spec says the resource, issuer and JWKS URLs SHALL use https. In tests/unit/test_config.py::test_invalid_values_stop_enterich_with_name_and_rule, only ISSUER and JWKS_URL get an http value to a non-loopback host. The only http RESOURCE_URL cases are http://127.0.0.1:80/mcp, which fails the canonical check whatever the scheme, and http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp, which is meant to load. I patched the call to reader.url("RESOURCE_URL", ...) to pass https_only=False, and load() then accepted ENTERICH_RESOURCE_URL=http://erp.example.com/mcp (checked in a scratch script). No config, main or app test sets an http resource URL to a non-loopback host.
proposal: Add ("RESOURCE_URL", "http://erp.example.com/mcp", HTTPS_ONLY) to the parametrized cases in test_invalid_values_stop_enterich_with_name_and_rule. The spec could also add it to the Definition of Done next to the issuer and JWKS http cases.

verdict.reason: REQ-002-PRS-NF005 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:163) says the resource, issuer and JWKS URLs SHALL use https, with plain http allowed only for a loopback host. Its Definition of Done (line 170) only gives http cases for the issuer and the JWKS URL. The resource URL check is in src/enterich/config.py:106: reader.url("RESOURCE_URL", canonical=True) uses the default https_only=True, and the rule itself is at config.py:268. In tests/unit/test_config.py:120-140 the only http RESOURCE_URL case is http://127.0.0.1:80/mcp, and the canonical rule stops it whatever the scheme. tests/unit/test_config.py:185 loads http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp, which is loopback, so it must load. tests/e2e never mentions the resource URL. I copied the repository to the scratchpad and changed config.py:106 to pass https_only=False. Then I ran pytest over tests/unit, tests/integration and tests/repo: 1369 passed and 1 failed. The failure is tests/repo/test_harness.py::test_the_sweep_finds_what_the_fourth_runs_survey_missed, a harness test that has nothing to do with config. No configuration, main, auth or service test noticed the https rule was gone. A first run with -x had stopped at tests/unit/test_erpnext.py::test_proxy_settings_in_the_environment_are_ignored on a ModuleNotFoundError in the copy's venv. That test passed on the second run, so it is not caused by the change. I did not run the harness test without the change, so I have not shown that it also fails on the unchanged code. The finding is confirmed as unproven: no test checks this. The fix is a test within the current spec: add ("RESOURCE_URL", "http://erp.example.com/mcp", HTTPS_ONLY) to the parametrized cases in tests/unit/test_config.py. A DoD wording change is optional and not needed.

claim: No test checks the guide's statement that the rights inherited through All and Desk User include none that posts or changes an accounting document. A Dependabot bump of the ERPNext image that adds such a right would leave the guide's deployment open unnoticed.
evidence: The guide's 'Inherited rights' bullet says None of them posts or changes an accounting document. In the pinned image, All and Desk User hold rules such as File create/write/delete, ToDo/Tag create/write/share, Workspace and Desktop Layout create/write/delete, Item select/share/export, and permlevel-1 read on Sales Invoice and POS Invoice. Today none of them writes an accounting DocType, but nothing pins that. tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py checks submit, cancel and delete only on the four drafted DocTypes. test_rights.py removes only rights listed in RIGHTS and never looks at the inherited roles. tests/repo/test_e2e.py:test_the_erpnext_services_run_one_image notes that Dependabot updates the image. So a new release giving Desk User write or create on, say, Account, Bank Transaction, Payment Request or Journal Entry would pass every test while the guide still says the deployment is closed.
proposal: Add an e2e test that reads, as Administrator, the DocPerm and Custom DocPerm rules for the roles All and Desk User. It asserts that none grants create, write, submit, cancel, amend or delete on a DocType of the Accounts, Selling, Buying, Stock or Setup modules (or compares them with a reviewed snapshot), so that an image bump changing them fails until the guide is checked again.

verdict.reason: docs/guides/configuration.md:66 ("Inherited rights") says the rights of All and Desk User include none that posts or changes an accounting document. SECURITY.md:29 puts in scope a guide whose instructions leave a deployment open. Its out-of-scope line (:33, ERPNext itself) covers bugs in ERPNext, not the guide's own claim about what ERPNext grants. REQ-002-PRS-NF013 (req-002-service.md:291) accepts these inherited rights on top of each row's rights but pins nothing about what they contain. I searched all of tests/ for 'Desk User', 'All', 'DocPerm', 'Custom DocPerm' and 'inherit'. The only hits are docstrings and comments in tests/e2e/test_rights.py (:4, :95). test_rights.py removes and checks only the rights listed in its RIGHTS rows, so a new inherited write or create on a DocType outside those rows changes no outcome. tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py checks submit, delete, cancel and changes to submitted documents and other people's drafts only on the four drafted DocTypes (Sales/Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Journal Entry). If an image release gave Desk User write or create on, say, Account, Bank Transaction or Payment Request, no test would fail. tests/repo/test_e2e.py:68 says Dependabot bumps that image. The backlog does not list this, and the specs don't say it is intended. The guide's claim can be checked: the DocPerm and Custom DocPerm rules for All and Desk User can be read on the e2e site and compared with a reviewed set, or asserted to hold no create, write, submit, cancel, amend or delete on accounting DocTypes. The test belongs with the ceiling tests (what ERPNext lets the agent user's key do directly), in tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py, and needs no change to the specs.

claim: No test applies the guide's site settings and checks that they exist and take effect. These are the User Permission on the company, `disable_document_sharing`, naming series for parties, `log_api_requests`, and the MCP switch. A setting the guide names wrongly, or one an ERPNext upgrade renames, goes unnoticed.
evidence: tests/e2e/seed.py:seed and seed.py:agent set up the company, the two roles, the role rules (permissions/rules) and the report roles (report_role), and nothing more. No User Permission is created, and no System, Selling or Buying Settings field is set (grep for `User Permission`, `disable_document_sharing`, `enable_mcp`, `log_api_requests` and naming under tests/ finds nothing). tests/repo/test_configuration_guide.py checks only that every ENTERICH_ variable is named in the guide. test_rights.py and test_ceiling.py run with the roles alone. So the guide's paragraph with the site settings could name a field that doesn't exist and every test would still pass. The `disable_mcp_server` breach above shows this happening. If ERPNext's default User Permission broke an operation, for example get_item on an Item whose Item Defaults name another company, that would go unnoticed as well.
proposal: Make the seed follow the guide's site settings: a default User Permission on COMPANY for the agent user, `disable_document_sharing` = 1, the naming series, `log_api_requests` = 1 and `enable_mcp` = 0. Add a tests/repo test that every settings field the guide names in backticks exists in the pinned image's DocType meta (or an e2e test that reads frappe.client.get_value for each one). Then test_rights proves the operations still work under the guide's full setup.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. A grep of all of tests/, including tests/e2e and tests/repo, for `disable_document_sharing`, `log_api_requests`, `disable_mcp`, `User Permission`, `naming_series`, `cust_master_name` and `supp_master_name` finds nothing.

The guide's "What the site must provide" section asks for these things: a default User Permission on the company (docs/guides/configuration.md:60), parties named by naming series (:78), `disable_document_sharing` (:79), `log_api_requests` (:81) and `disable_mcp_server` (:82). The seed (tests/e2e/seed.py) creates none of them. Its seed, company, agent, permissions, rules and report_role (lines 198-415) set up only the company, the roles, the DocPerm rules and the report roles. tests/repo/test_configuration_guide.py only checks that every ENTERICH_ variable is named in the guide. test_rights.py and test_ceiling.py run with the roles alone.

So if one of these field names were removed, misspelled or renamed by an ERPNext upgrade, every test would still pass. Nothing would notice either if the default User Permission stopped an operation from working.

The finding is in scope. SECURITY.md:29 covers "a guide whose instructions leave a deployment open". If a sharing or MCP switch the guide names doesn't exist on the site, that deployment is left open. docs/backlog/backlog.md lists nothing about it, and no spec says it is intended.

I chose fix rather than proposal because REQ-002-PRS-NF013's Definition of Done already asks that each operation work for an agent user set up with exactly the listed rights, and the guide's User Permission belongs to that setup. The fix is to make the seed apply the guide's site settings and to check against the pinned v16 site that each named settings field exists. That needs no change to the specs or ADRs.

The local end-to-end site isn't running, so I couldn't check here which of the named fields really exist. The finding's mutants list is empty.

claim: A return draft's create posts ERPNext's own mapped return almost as it comes back. Only the forced `docstatus: 0` stands between that mapping and a body that posts, and nothing at all stops `amended_from`. No test gives Enterich a mapping that carries either field, so the tests would miss this guard being removed or never being added.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/returns.py:create builds `doc = {**mapped, "items": lines, ...}` from `return_of`. `_plain` (returns.py:52) drops only `name`, `owner` and keys starting with `__` (DROPPED, returns.py:16). drafts.insert (drafts.py:132-134) then sends `{**doc, "company": ..., "docstatus": 0}`. So `docstatus` is overwritten, but an `amended_from` in ERPNext's answer goes into the POST to /api/resource/Sales Invoice or Purchase Invoice. REQ-001-URS-F003's notes and tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py::test_a_cancelled_document_is_amended_with_create_alone say that only Enterich's code closes this door. The DoD of REQ-001-PRS-F006 (req-001-core.md:277) says no call sends a document with `amended_from`. Today stock ERPNext keeps the promise, not Enterich: `amended_from` is `no_copy: 1` on both invoice DocTypes, so frappe/model/mapper.py leaves it out. A Property Setter or an app that overrides make_sales_return or make_debit_note would bring it back unnoticed. Tests: the fake's mapped_return (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:584) copies every field of the invoice and sets `docstatus: 0`. No fixture invoice has `amended_from`, and none returns a mapping with `docstatus` other than 0. So the door check in tests/integration/conftest.py:32 (`fake.doors == []`) never sees either case. Two changes would pass every test: dropping `"docstatus": 0` from insert, or writing it as `{"docstatus": 0, **doc}`. The invoice-create tests that check the exact body catch neither for returns, and returns are the only path where the body comes from ERPNext.
proposal: Test: in tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py, make the fake's mapped return for one invoice carry `amended_from: <a cancelled invoice>` and `docstatus: 1`, then call create_draft_sales_return and create_draft_purchase_return. Assert that the POST body has `docstatus` 0 and no `amended_from`, and that `fake.doors == []`. Change: have drafts.insert (the one write path for every create) drop `amended_from` next to forcing `docstatus: 0`, or add it to returns.DROPPED. Then Enterich keeps the promise itself instead of leaving it to ERPNext's no_copy setting.

verdict.reproduction: I tested in copies of the repo under the scratchpad (m1, m2). Two mutants of drafts.insert (src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:132-134) ran against tests/unit and tests/integration. (a) Dropping `"docstatus": 0` is caught: tests/integration/test_bank_and_cash_drafts.py::test_a_receipt_sends_exactly_the_catalogued_body fails. (b) Writing it as `{"docstatus": 0, **doc, "company": ...}` survives: 1093 passed. A throwaway probe, tests/integration/test_zz_probe.py in the copies, drove create_draft_sales_return through the integration client and FakeErpnext. With unmodified HEAD code and `amended_from` set on the invoice, which the fake's mapped_return copies into the mapping, Enterich POSTed /api/resource/Sales Invoice with amended_from=ACC-SINV-2026-00004. The fake flagged it as a door ("a document with amended_from"). So nothing in Enterich strips the field; only ERPNext's no_copy keeps it out today. A second probe gave a mapping with docstatus 1. HEAD sent docstatus 0, but mutant (b) sent docstatus 1 and the probe caught it. No existing test sets either field.
verdict.reason: returns.py:16 DROPPED is {name, owner}, and _plain (returns.py:52) also drops only `__` keys, so an `amended_from` in ERPNext's mapped return reaches drafts.insert (drafts.py:132-134) and the POST unchanged. The probe shows it. REQ-001-PRS-F006's DoD (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:277) says no call sends a document with `amended_from`, and req-001-core.md:122 notes that create alone amends a cancelled document. The fake's mapped_return (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:584) always sets docstatus 0, and no fixture carries amended_from. The conftest door check (tests/integration/conftest.py:32) would catch both cases but never meets them; no test in tests/ sets amended_from outside test_tool_list's direct door list. One part of the finding is wrong: removing `"docstatus": 0` outright is killed by the exact-body tests of the other creates (test_a_receipt_sends_exactly_the_catalogued_body). The reordered override survives the whole suite, though, and the amended_from gap is real. The fix stays within the current specs: a test in tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py whose mapped return carries amended_from and docstatus 1, plus a code change that strips amended_from (returns.DROPPED or drafts.insert). I set pattern to null: the field is passed through when it should be stripped, which is not a dropped argument.

claim: A return draft sends ERPNext's whole mapped return back to ERPNext with only `name`, `owner` and `__*` keys removed, so whether the inserted document carries `amended_from` depends on ERPNext's mapping, not on Enterich, and no test returns an amended invoice.
evidence: returns.create (src/enterich/tools/returns.py:233) builds `doc = {**mapped, "items": lines, ...}` from `_plain(await context.erpnext.return_of(...))`, and DROPPED (line 15) is only {name, owner}. drafts.insert (src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:132-134) forces `docstatus: 0`, but nothing removes `amended_from`. tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py::test_a_cancelled_document_is_amended_with_create_alone shows the role ceiling doesn't stop an amendment, so not sending `amended_from` is the only guard. Standard ERPNext leaves it out of the mapping because the field is no_copy, but a site whose mapping copies it (for example a Property Setter on no_copy) would have Enterich POST a Sales or Purchase Invoice with `amended_from` set, breaking the DoD's 'no ERPNext call Enterich makes sends a document ... with amended_from'. The fake's mapped_return (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:599-600) copies every field of the invoice and the door detector (line 1049) would flag it. claim: No test notices if the draft comment gets its own full OPERATION_TIMEOUT instead of what remains of the operation's 60 seconds, which would let one create or update run up to about 120 s.

claim: REQ-001-PRS-F013's first Definition of Done item says the integration suite calls every operation with a client that never confirms anything, and no test checks this, so an operation with no call through the confirm-nothing Session would go unnoticed.
evidence: In practice the promise rests on the transport. src/enterich/app.py:create_app sets stateless_http=True and json_response=True, so there is no channel back to the client for elicitation or sampling. src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:_tool uses the SDK request only for request_id, and _annotations (lines 151-161) only publishes hints; no code reads them. Those settings are guarded: tests/integration/test_service.py::test_initialize_and_list_tools checks for a JSON content type, test_no_session_state_between_processes checks statelessness, and Session._rpc's response.json() would fail on an SSE answer. A tool that tried to elicit would raise or time out into a refusal, and that operation's own tests would fail. What nothing checks is that every operation is reached through tests/integration/mcp.py:Session, the client that 'never confirms anything (REQ-001-PRS-F013)'. The promise record lists no test citing REQ-001-PRS-F013 ('tests': [], 'tests_by_section': []). tests/integration/conftest.py and tests/repo/ have no check that the tool names called during the integration suite equal enterich.tools.names(). Today all 37 operations appear in tests/integration, by a name count. A new operation added to an OPERATIONS list, or an existing one whose integration tests are moved to unit tests that call op.run directly, would ship without this DoD and every test would still pass.
proposal: Add a session-scoped record of the tool names Session.call sends, plus a check at the end of the integration run, or a tests/repo test that collects the names called in tests/integration, asserting that they equal set(enterich.tools.names()). Seeing a refusal case for every operation is enough; the strict schema refuses empty arguments. Cite REQ-001-PRS-F013 in the test so the inventory links the requirement to it.

verdict.reason: REQ-001-PRS-F013's first DoD item (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:369) says the integration suite calls every operation with a client that never confirms anything. tests/integration/mcp.py:49-51 says its Session is that client, but nothing checks that every operation is called through it.
